question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I first searched for the task terms, but those searches did not surface the style vocabulary, so I used the vocabulary index. It gave paths for C# style choices and tiers. I requested both paths before viewing either response, expecting the choices to hold IDs and properties and the tiers to hold descriptions. The choices response already embedded the tier descriptions, so the separate tier request proved redundant. I inspected the full choices response, then filtered its scope, map coverage, Boolean property sets, conflict groups, member IDs, and embedded tiers. That showed five complete-data, byte-preserving, endorsed choices and both declared groups. I stopped when those facts and the scope metadata answered the task; another schema or link read did not promise a specific missing fact. I treated incomplete or unavailable property cases as hypothetical limits and did not infer CLI invocation syntax.
